meta.description: Where the figures on this site come from, how we measure them, and what they don't tell you.

title: Method and <0>limitations</0>
intro: This site shows figures. Here you can read where they come from, how we measure them and what they don't tell you.

wat.title: What we measure
wat.intro: We measure two things: how participants feel and work before and after the training, and what they notice themselves at the end.
items: Productivity, with the World Health Organization's Health and Work Performance Questionnaire (HPQ).
Stress, with the Perceived Stress Scale.
What participants notice: a short survey at the end, asking in which areas they see improvement.

hoe.title: How we measure
hoe.text: Participants fill in a questionnaire themselves: once before the training and once 4 weeks after it ends. They fill in the end-of-training evaluation once. So every figure is self-reported: it is how participants experience it. We report the results for the group. Individual answers never go to the employer.

periode.title: Period
periode.text: Each figure says when it was measured. We check every figure at least once a year. If a check is more than 12 months old, we look again before the figure stays online.

beperkingen.title: Limitations
items: There is no control group. We compare participants with themselves, before and after. So we can't say whether a change was caused by the training. That's why we write 'after the training', never 'because of the training'.

At TheyDo, a small group that didn't take part also filled in the questionnaires (6 people). Their productivity went up too, by 13.5%. That group is too small to compare with, but you should know it exists.
Everything is self-reported. People who have just finished a training often rate its effect more positively.
Not everyone fills in the evaluation. At TheyDo, 22 of the 39 participants did. The people who answer may be more positive than those who don't.
The groups are small. One person more or less can move a percentage by several points.
Results differ per organisation. What happened at one organisation is no guarantee for another.
